title: Authority boundary: Deployment owns state reconciliation, not application meaning
summary: Deployment owns discovery, capability assessment, artifact/runtime/configuration placement, planning, execution, verification, launch preparation, evidence and rollback information. It does not own business/application semantics, scheduling, worker allocation or result interpretation.
invariants: Deployment may execute an application-declared verification command but interprets only declared deployment success/failure outputs.
Scheduling and Job-to-Node placement remain external authorities.
A consumer can add requirements/adapters without subclassing the whole engine.
Unknown application metadata remains opaque to Deployment.

provenance.claim: Enumerates what Deployment owns and explicitly does not own.
Manifest is declarative and application metadata remains opaque.
Applications extend deployment through ordinary requirements rather than replacing the engine.
